title: Minimum Railway Platforms
statement:
A railway station receives `n` trains in one day. Train `i` arrives at time `arrival[i]` and leaves at time `departure[i]`, where `arrival[i] ≤ departure[i]`. Times are plain integers.

A train occupies its platform for the whole closed interval from `arrival[i]` to `departure[i]`, **including both end points**. So if one train departs at time `t` and another arrives at time `t`, they are on the platforms at the same moment and need different platforms. A platform can serve any number of trains in a day, as long as their intervals do not share a moment.

Find the minimum number of platforms the station needs so that no train ever has to wait.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `arrival[0..n-1]`.
The third line contains `n` integers `departure[0..n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum number of platforms.

examples.explanation: At time 15 the first train (10..20), the second (12..18) and the third (15..45) are all in the station, so 3 platforms are needed. At no time are more than 3 trains present.
Each train leaves exactly when the next one arrives. Since both end points are included, the trains at times 5 and 9 overlap, but no three trains meet at one moment, so 2 platforms are enough.
The trains never overlap, so one platform is enough.

hints: The answer is the largest number of trains that are in the station at the same moment.
Sort the arrival times and the departure times separately. You do not need to keep track of which arrival belongs to which departure.

Sweep both sorted lists with two pointers: an arrival (that happens no later than the next departure) adds a platform, otherwise a departure frees one. Be careful with ties, since an arrival at the same time as a departure counts as overlapping.
